query: I just finished implementing the caching layer for phase 2. Before I mark it done, can you review the code in src/cache/ for anything over-engineered or unnecessarily complex? I want to make sure we're not shipping bloat.

Look at the error handling in lib/api-client.ts — every single function has a try-catch that logs, wraps in a custom error class, then re-throws. Claude generated most of this. Can you strip out the redundant error wrapping and simplify the patterns across all 12 endpoint files?

The processOrder function in services/order.go is 87 lines long with 5 levels of nesting. I need you to break it apart into smaller functions and flatten the conditionals. Also check if the sister function processRefund has the same problem.

We have an AbstractBaseValidatorFactory interface in src/validation/ that only has one concrete implementation. I also see a ValidatorStrategy, ValidatorBuilder, and ValidatorRegistry that all seem to exist for no reason. Can you collapse this down to just what we need?

I notice that the same 15-line block for parsing config and setting defaults appears in main.go, server.go, and worker.go. Can you extract that into a shared helper and remove the duplication? Then check if there are other copy-pasted blocks I'm missing.

After the AI generated our auth module, I see typeof checks on every parameter even though we're using TypeScript with strict mode. There are also null checks after non-nullable destructuring. Go through src/auth/ and remove all the redundant runtime type guards that TypeScript already handles.

There's dead code all over the place in our utils/ directory — functions that aren't imported anywhere, commented-out blocks from 6 months ago, and feature flags for experiments we shipped last quarter. Can you do a thorough cleanup pass and remove everything unused?

I just reviewed the PR diff and the new middleware chain feels way too clever. There's a dynamic dispatch system with reflection when a simple switch statement would work. Can you simplify the routing middleware in pkg/http/middleware.go to use straightforward conditionals instead?

Before I close out this phase, run through the 4 files I changed (parser.py, tokenizer.py, evaluator.py, compiler.py) and tell me if any of them have functions that are too long, unnecessary abstractions, or patterns that could be simplified. I want clean code before we move on.

The formatOutput function has a chain of 8 if-else blocks that each call a nearly identical formatting helper with slightly different args. Can you refactor this into a data-driven approach — maybe a config map — and eliminate the repetition? Files are in src/output/.
I need to add a new caching layer to our API. Can you design the architecture for an in-memory cache with Redis fallback, including the interface definitions and factory pattern we should use?
Can you help me write a complex regex that validates international phone numbers including country codes, optional parentheses around area codes, and handles both spaces and dashes as separators?
Our test suite is taking 14 minutes to run. Can you profile the slowest tests in test/integration/ and figure out what's causing the bottleneck? I suspect it's the database setup/teardown.

I need to implement retry logic with exponential backoff and jitter for our HTTP client. The current code just fails on the first timeout. Can you add robust error handling with configurable retry counts?
Write a migration script that restructures our users table to support multi-tenancy. We need to add tenant_id columns, backfill existing data, and update all the foreign key constraints.

Help me debug why the WebSocket connection drops after exactly 60 seconds in production but works fine locally. Check the nginx config, the Node server timeout settings, and the client-side keepalive implementation.
Can you set up our CI pipeline to run linting, unit tests, integration tests, and deploy to staging? We're using GitHub Actions and need matrix builds for Node 18 and 20.

I want to add comprehensive error handling to our payment processing flow. Right now failures just crash silently. Add try-catch blocks, custom error types, logging, and user-facing error messages throughout src/payments/.
Can you explain how the visitor pattern works and whether it would be a good fit for our AST transformation pipeline? I'm comparing it against a simple recursive approach.
Review our API endpoint for security vulnerabilities — check for SQL injection, XSS, CSRF, missing auth checks, and rate limiting gaps in the routes/ directory.
